native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB: In the 17th century BCE (1700-1601 BCE) the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses (ZKeform: +0.74 -> -1.13; DeltaPF = -1.87) and the Diversity in Pottery Decoration simultaneously rises (Zkeverz: -0.48 -> +0.97; DeltaPD = +1.45; cross-metric S = +3.32). Per the operational conventions adopted in this study, the century label uses the start-inclusive / upper-edge convention: a bin whose lower edge starts at BCE=1700 is the 17th century BCE, covering 1700-1601 BCE; calBP and CE are sign-flipped to BCE (BCE = -CE; calBP used only as a sanity audit). All four method variants (capital.csv level 100-year grid, time_series_data interpolated curve at century start, time_series_data 200-year centered diff, and raw-anchor diff over the 37 sparse anchors) identify the same 1700 BCE bin as the unique century in 4300-500 BCE that simultaneously satisfies DeltaPF<0 AND DeltaPD>0 with non-trivial magnitude. The capital.csv `group` label attached to the BCE=1700 row is LN (Late Neolithic); the next century (1600-1501 BCE) is OBA, so the collapse-and-rise event sits at the cusp of LN->OBA in this dataset. Caveats: the time_series_data pottery columns contain only 37 raw anchors across 3600 yearly rows so the `_inter` curves are piecewise-linear and flattens within-century variability; the substantive answer relies on the level values directly stored in capital.csv (-1.13 and +0.97 for Form and Decoration at the start of the 17th c. BCE); switching to an upper-edge convention would relabel the bin to "18th century BCE" without changing the numbers.
